object_description: two interlocking courtyard volumes of different heights
design_condition: The two differently oriented and differently tall volumes follow the site geometries and slope, preserving the northern garden and historic ensemble while forming a southern entrance recess and layered links to the park.

positive.statement: The two interlocking buildings fit judiciously into the site through differentiated orientation and height.
The large central staircase creates a beautiful articulation between the two buildings.
The two patios facilitate orientation and bring natural light into the building.
The private floors are well organized and allow wandering around in a loop.
The relationship with the historic park is of quality and forms a homogeneous landscape and architectural ensemble.
The arrangement offers diverse openings toward the large landscape and preserves the protected trees.

negative.statement: The three-story building over the parking creates an unclear vertical layout and complicates movement to the collective spaces.
The shared landing between the staircase and elevator leads to serious logistical conflicts.
The access to the living spaces is too small and eccentrically positioned.
The privacy of rooms along the upper access path remains questionable.
The generous spaces are sometimes excessive, undermining the compactness of the general organization.
The building's large volume produces reduced outdoor spaces lacking in quality.
The considerable excavation generates a significant investment and worsens the biodiversity balance.
The car flow from the underground parking conflicts directly with the main entrance.
The extensive footprint makes the ensemble massive and oversized compared with the castle and village houses.
The clearance spaces in front of the cafeteria are limited by the road.
The south entrance needs to be revisited to give the place more character and clarify its purpose.
The project is more than 30 percent above the most economical proposal in total cost.
